business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Dilutive Revenue-Based Financing for Digital Brands

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Double Tax Avoidance Agreements with multiple jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (S.C. 2000, c. 17) and FINTRAC Guidelines; British Columbia Limited Partnership Act, SBC 2022, c. 5, and related regulations for UBO disclosure
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and Canadian sanctions screening protocols including FINTRAC's AML/CFT standards and adverse media checks

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English language requirements with compliance to Canadian naming conventions and no prohibited words without approval
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names that are identical or deceptively similar to registered entities
Restricted terms such as 'bank', 'credit union', 'insurance' without prior approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit written appeal to BC Registry Services within the prescribed period, detailing grounds for reconsideration and supporting evidence

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for Limited Partnerships provided registered office is maintained and commercial substance is demonstrated for tax and regulatory purposes
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; British Columbia Registry Services conducts targeted inspections rather than unannounced physical visits for pre-incorporation entities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and name clearance services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border corporate setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO beneficial ownership profiling and screening
Document notarization, apostille, and legalization services
Registered office and address compliance setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: British Columbia Limited Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 294, as amended, particularly ss. 2–9 (formation and registration), ss. 12–20 (limited partners, contributions and withdrawal), s. 23 (records), and ss. 45–52 (duties of general partner and dissolution); where the general partner is a BC corporation, Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 127 and 254–259.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registry Services – Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Victoria, British Columbia; filings submitted through the BC Registry Online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: LP Form 1 – Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (under the Limited Partnership Act), leading to issuance of the Certificate of Limited Partnership by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a British Columbia limited partnership. Capital contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement; limited partners' withdrawal of capital is restricted under s. 18 of the Limited Partnership Act to preserve limited liability. No escrow account or capital deposit duty is imposed by the BC Corporate Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Corporation, as sole general partner, accepts the capital subscriptions of each limited partner of the Fund as set forth in the Subscription Schedule and directs that all contributions be deposited into the Fund's segregated operating account; (2) The registered office and records office of the Fund are hereby established at 1000 Burrard Street, Vancouver, British Columbia, and the registered agent consents to service; (3) Marie-Claire Dufort is appointed General Manager and Chief Compliance Officer, and she is authorized to execute and submit the Application for Registration of Limited Partnership, to engage counsel and accountants, and to open and manage the Fund's bank accounts; (4) The Fund's fiscal year end is December 31.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services – Corporate Registry (BC Registry Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online Name Request using BC Registry Online. Conduct a NUANS pre-screen to ensure the proposed name, including the phrase 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.', is distinctive and not confusing with any existing BC or extraprovincial entity. Pay the prescribed name-reservation fee and record the resulting Name Reservation Number, which is valid for a statutory period.
required_dossiers: Government-issued photo identification of the applicant
Statement of justification for any name without a prescribed distinctive element
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an amended Name Request with a new distinctive element, or submit a written consent from any conflicting entity; the reservation fee is not refundable and the re-filing fee must be paid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and General Partner Authorizing Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and board of directors of the corporate general partner (private act, not a government filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA), setting out capital commitments, profit allocation, transfer restrictions, and dissolution terms. Have the sole corporate general partner adopt the pro forma first board resolution authorizing the creation of the LP, appointment of officers, and execution of all registrations. Retain original executed copies.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution of the corporate General Partner
Subscription and capital commitment letters of limited partners
Certificate of incumbency and good standing of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the authority of signatories, provide a certified extract of the board resolution and incumbency certificate; if the LPA is ineffective, the board may adopt a ratifying resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Registration of Limited Partnership and Appointment of Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registry Services (BC Registry Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LP1) online. Provide the proposed LP name, Name Reservation Number, British Columbia registered office address, and consent of the registered agent. Upon review, the Registry issues the Certificate of Limited Partnership. The certificate is conclusive evidence of formation.
required_dossiers: LP Form 1 – Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership
Consent to Act as Registered Agent
Identity and address of each general partner and limited partner (where the Registry requires disclosure)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a deficiency notice, file an amended or supplemental statement through BC Registry Online within the response period. If registration is refused due to non-compliance, correct the defect and re-file; if the certificate is revoked, obtain reinstatement under the LP Act after paying arrears and filing updated information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration (online / eFile / My Business Account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the LP certificate is issued, register the partnership for a Business Number using online Business Registration or Form RC460. Select the income tax (TX) account, GST/HST (RT) registration if taxable supplies exceed C$30,000, and payroll (RP) if employees are hired. Submit the partnership's name, business address, general partner information, and stated ISIC/NAICS classification (6499/525990).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA sends a clarification letter, respond within the specified deadline with a revised RC460 and supporting partnership documents; if the BN is cancelled, re-apply using the same legal name and provide evidence of continued existence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and WorkSafeBC Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Licensing Division (e.g. City of Vancouver) and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence for the British Columbia office, describing the business as 'royalty and revenue-based financing fund'. If the fund employs workers, register with WorkSafeBC as an employer and obtain a clearance letter for the assigned classification code. Confirm that the fund's activity does not constitute deposit-taking or a 'security' requiring BC Securities Act registration; retain a legal opinion to that effect.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership and CRA Business Number
Lease agreement or proof of premises
WorkSafeBC Employer Registration Form and payroll detail
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality conditions the licence on zoning compliance, submit landlord's authorization or obtain a discretionary development permit; if WorkSafeBC assigns a wrong industry classification, request a reclassification review within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable (no manufacturing or industrial board for ISIC 6499); relevant authority for physical premises is the municipal licensing division (e.g. City of Vancouver Business Licensing Office) together with WorkSafeBC for occupational compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence for Non-Dilutive Revenue-Based Financing Fund

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA study required for pure office-based financing operation; the business occupies no industrial facility and introduces no prescribed contamination source
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No discharge permits or VOC/wastewater standards apply to the financing activity. General duty compliance applies: any office-generated hazardous waste must be managed under the BC Environmental Management Act, Hazardous Waste Regulation, and the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999. If a physical manufacturing affiliate is created, a full EIA and provincial discharge authorization would be triggered under the BC Water Sustainability Act and applicable federal thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire marshal / Vancouver Fire Rescue Services; municipal structural load inspection and occupancy clearance for the leased office; WorkSafeBC registration and Site Compliance Clearance; occupational health and safety orientation for all employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal taxation; electronic portal: CRA My Business Account (www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) is administered separately by the BC Ministry of Finance through the OneStop BC portal (www.onestop.gov.bc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident and domestic limited partnerships apply for a federal Business Number (BN) using the Business Registration Online (BRO) service or Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts.' CRA issues a 9-digit BN and a GST/HST program account bearing the two-letter identifier 'RT.' The BC Registrar of Companies first registers the limited partnership under the Partnership Act (BC); Form RC1 must attach the BC certificate of registration, the partnership agreement, and, for non-resident partners, Form RC464A (Non-Resident Partnership Information Return). Because the LP is fiscally transparent, no corporate income-tax program account (RC) is opened for the partnership itself; the LP files an annual T5013 Information Return and T5013 slips, while each partner reports its allocable share under its own TIN/BN. GST/HST registration becomes mandatory once taxable supplies in Canada reach the CAD 30,000 threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — a BC limited partnership is fiscally transparent under s.96 of the Income Tax Act (Canada). Partnership income, deductions, and tax credits are allocated to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement. For GST/HST purposes, however, the LP is a separate 'person' registrant under the Excise Tax Act (Canada).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian equivalent of a check-the-box election exists; transparency is mandatory for income tax purposes. Available elections include: (i) a s.249(8) ITA election permitting a non-calendar fiscal period; (ii) a GST/HST Quick Method election for small suppliers with worldwide taxable supplies under CAD 400,000; (iii) Canada–US Treaty Article IV(6) relief for fiscally transparent entities, enabling US partners to claim treaty benefits on allocated shares; and (iv) a US check-the-box election via Form 8832 to treat the BC LP as an association or corporation for US federal tax purposes, which may create hybrid-mismatch exposure constrained by ITA ss.18.2–18.4 (OECD BEPS Action 2 implementation).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) (federal, 5%); Harmonized Sales Tax does not apply in British Columbia. BC imposes a parallel 7% Provincial Sales Tax (PST) on taxable consumption, separate from GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or total supplies exceeding CAD 30,000 over the last four consecutive calendar quarters. For non-resident suppliers, the threshold is tested against taxable supplies made in Canada; registration is mandatory once exceeded and voluntary below the threshold to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, transaction-control APIs, or digital stamping. CRA accepts paper and PDF invoices and maintains a voluntary Pan-Canadian Trust Framework pilot for PEPPOL BIS e-invoicing (business-to-government). Registrants must issue GST/HST invoices containing the BN (RT program account), the GST amount charged or a zero-rating notation, and the supplier's name. Tax records must be kept in machine-readable format for six years under ETA s.286(1); GST/HST returns are filed electronically using XML or CRA-supported EDI channels.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for: (1) exports of tangible personal property in respect of which title is transferred and goods are physically exported from Canada by the supplier; (2) services supplied to a non-resident person who is not registered for GST/HST and who is outside Canada when receiving the supply (ETA Sch. VI Pt V s.7), excluding supplies in respect of Canadian real property or goods used in Canada; and (3) financial services supplied to non-residents (including revenue-interest participation financing and royalty funding) under ETA Sch. VI Pt VII, subject to prescribed exceptions for payment-card issuance and payment-clearing services. Royalty and financing streams generated from non-resident digital-brand counterparties must satisfy the non-resident-ordinarily-resident and non-use-in-Canada conditions to attract the 0% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration via CBSA: B13A (paper) or Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED)/electronic declaration for controlled or regulated goods
Commercial invoice or fully executed royalty-financing term sheet identifying the non-resident payor, revenue-interest royalty rate, and waterfall calculation
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CBSA-approved carrier manifest evidencing physical export of any goods collateral
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/SWIFT statements evidencing the receipt of export consideration in Canadian dollars from the non-resident payor
Non-resident status evidence: certificate of foreign registration, Forms W-8BEN-E/W-8IMY, tax-residency certificates, and beneficial-ownership records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and CBSA audit export zero-rating through document-to-payment reconstruction. Failure to evidence export delivery and receipt of consideration from a non-resident within 180 days of invoice date results in reclassification to a taxable supply, reassessment of net GST at 5%, denial of input tax credits, and statutory interest. The CRA additionally asserts penalties under the Excise Tax Act, including: failure-to-register and failure-to-collect penalties equal to 100% of the tax at issue; general non-compliance penalties up to CAD 100,000 per offence (ETA s.281.1); false-statement penalties of 25% of tax avoided where zero-rating is unsupported; and, on criminal summary conviction, fines up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment up to two years (ETA s.327.2). The four-year reassessment period is extended to seven years for misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud (ITA s.152(4)). BC PST enforcement applies separate clawback and 25% penalty exposure under the Provincial Sales Tax Act (BC).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Department of Finance Canada and Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); BC Financial Services Authority supervises provincial financial services providers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full currency convertibility under IMF Article VIII obligations. There are no exchange controls, no advance approvals on current or capital account transactions, and no restrictions on converting CAD into foreign currency. Capital contributions, loan repayments, royalties, dividends, and branch profits may be freely remitted; however, Part XIII withholding tax on non-resident passive income and transfer-pricing documentation requirements apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds. Exporters may retain receipts in CAD or foreign currency accounts without government intervention. FINTRAC reporting obligations apply to cross-border electronic funds transfers exceeding CAD 10,000, and authorized dealers must report balance-of-payments data to Statistics Canada / Bank of Canada.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for Canadian-registered payment service providers and OSFI-regulated fintech platforms; Low for offshore digital EMIs without a Canadian presence, as the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) requires PSP registration and major banks generally require domestic settlement accounts and local addresses for corporate clients.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks permit fully remote account opening in many cases, but enhanced due diligence for a Limited Partnership typically requires at least one general partner or authorized signing officer to attend a secure video interview. Physical proof of identity, notarized LP agreement, Certificate of Limited Partnership, and apostilled corporate documents are standard; pure remote opening without documentary confirmation is rare for cross-border royalty funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership chain of a limited partnership involving non-resident limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete register of limited partners, LLC/LLP ownership chart, certified LP agreement, Certificate of Limited Partnership, UBO declarations with passport copies, and tax residence confirmations for all beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or inactive Canadian Business Number (BN) / provincial incorporation records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Active BC Business Number registration, BC Corporate Registry search report, good-standing certificate, audited financial statements or initial funding evidence, and original board/partner resolutions authorizing account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds derived from royalty receivables or revenue-based financing contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed royalty financing agreements, receivables schedules, bank statements showing counterparty payments, independent audit confirmations, and a clear explanation of the commercial purpose for each projected inflow/outflow.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: No exchange-control approval is required. Inbound contributions should be remitted by SWIFT MT103 to the Canadian operating account with the payment purpose statement 'capital contribution to Limited Partnership' in Field 70. The remitter must provide full legal name, address, and UBO details to satisfy FINTRAC large-value reporting when the transaction exceeds CAD 10,000. For treaty-compliant transactions, ensure the investing entity provides a Canadian non-resident form (e.g., NR301) where relevant.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements and royalty disbursements should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 for standard cross-border wires; documentary trade settlements may use SWIFT MT700/MT760 (letters of credit) or MT707 amendments. Domestic disbursements can be cleared via ACH/NACHA, EFT, or wire transfer. All outbound flows must be screened against OFAC, Canada UN sanctions, and FINTRAC suspicious transaction reporting rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) when offered by Canadian authorized dealers for exotic currency exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies – BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 45 calendar days after the anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration in British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 50 (approx. USD 37) applied to filings submitted after the 45-day deadline; failure to file annual report for two consecutive years may result in an administrative strike-off after Notice of Intent is published by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year partnership, by March 31 following the fiscal year end; for a non-calendar year-end, within five months after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 under Income Tax Act s. 162; additional penalties apply for gross negligence and for failure to file required schedules.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit threshold under the BC Limited Partnership Act for a private limited partnership carrying on non-dilutive royalty financing; an audit is required only when (i) stipulated in the limited partnership agreement, (ii) requested by limited partners under the partnership agreement or BC Partnership Act, (iii) ordered by a court, or (iv) the LP is subject to securities legislation as a reporting issuer or another regulated financial framework.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Canada if the LP is a reporting issuer or required by investors/lenders; otherwise Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) in Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LP must keep a current register of partners showing contributions, withdrawals, and transfers. Transfers of partnership interests are recorded in the register within 30 days and are confirmed annually via the BC annual report confirmation filed with the Registrar of Companies; no separate UBO filing is prescribed for BC limited partnerships.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (limited partners' contributions and transfers)
Register of Assignments (transfers of partnership interests)
Minute Book (general partner resolutions and meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110 – 370 per year (CAD 150 – 500 per year) for registered office and records agent services in British Columbia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,700 – 18,500 per year (CAD 5,000 – 25,000 per year) for a certified audit of a private royalty financing limited partnership

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Not applicable; Limited Partnership is a pass-through entity, income allocated to partners. No statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions for this entity type.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 (Partnership Information Return) filed via CRA's electronic filing system (eFILE or Internet File Transfer)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., if year-end Dec 31, due May 31)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full legal name and registered office address in Canada; if no Canadian address, use the address of the designated partner or agent.
If the partnership has no BN, obtain one from CRA; non-resident partners must ensure the BN is registered for the partnership.
Enter the fiscal year-end as per the partnership agreement; must be a consistent annual date.
Report each partner's share of income/loss based on the partnership agreement; non-resident partners must provide their tax residency and identification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: CAD 25 per day for each partner, up to CAD 2,500 per partner; additional penalties for failure to provide information (up to CAD 100 per day, max CAD 2,500).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (statutory rate for dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-residents; for LP distributions, withholding may apply on certain income, but not on return of capital)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, non-resident partners must file Form NR301 (Certificate of Residence) and submit Form NR302 or NR303 to the partnership. The partnership must retain these forms and apply the reduced withholding rate if the treaty provides for it.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, treaty reduced to 10% (e.g., under US-Canada treaty) or 0% for certain types; Interest: statutory 25%, treaty reduced to 0% (e.g., US) or 10% for some jurisdictions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 5,000,000 for non-service transactions; CAD 1,000,000 for services
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) like offshore jurisdictions; however, general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles apply. For treaty benefits, the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) under BEPS may be invoked.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate misrepresentation of income or expenses, or concealment of assets to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fines up to 200% of tax evaded, up to CAD 200,000, and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they knowingly participated in the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a shell entity without economic substance to artificially shift profits or avoid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment, penalties up to 50% of tax avoided, and potential criminal charges for fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties and reassessed taxes if they directed the arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with AML reporting requirements, such as not reporting suspicious transactions or not maintaining required records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CAD 2 million for individuals, CAD 10 million for entities, and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for fines if they knowingly failed to implement AML controls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain transfer pricing documentation or not applying the arm's length principle in cross-border transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment, plus interest on the additional tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing arrangements.
